title: Quality control and handover
audience: Trainee or new worker on the pressure cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Capture before/after evidence, waste records, client sign-off, limitations, property defects and incidents.
referencesAtStart: Official sources used in this lesson (dates as shown on each page): Safe Work Australia, Working at heights (no date shown); SafeWork NSW, Work safely at heights in construction (no date shown); SafeWork NSW, High risk work licences (15 June 2026); WorkSafe Victoria, High risk work licence (reviewed 30 June 2026); SafeWork SA, Lowering the height threshold will raise safety standards (news, 5 June 2026); WorkSafe Queensland, Boom-type elevating work platform (no date shown); WorkSafe WA, Boom-type elevating work platform licence class (published 11 August 2026; updated 13 August 2026); WorkSafe Tasmania, Check the classes (updated 1 December 2023); Access Canberra (ACT Government), High risk work licences (no publication date); NT WorkSafe, Elevating work platform licence bulletin (no date shown); WA Consumer Protection, Estimates, quotes and deposits (updated 4 September 2026); Northern Territory Government, Quotes and estimates (no date shown); NSW Government, Electrical licences and certificates (building and trades) (updated 23 June 2026).

instruction.heading: Pressure cleaning at height and the access context
instruction.body: This lesson sits in the pressure cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level pressure work and work that is elevated or on a roof, so falls, high-pressure water, hoses, electrical supply and exhaust gas are all hazards that the inspection and handover can reveal. Safe Work Australia treats construction work with a fall risk of more than 2 metres as high risk construction work. NSW requires a safe work method statement where a fall could exceed 2 metres. In South Australia, construction work with a risk of falling more than two metres is high-risk from 1 July 2026, according to SafeWork SA's guidance (March 2026, no day shown); the regulation text was not read in this pass. The Victorian, Queensland, Western Australian and Tasmanian pages checked do not state a metre threshold for this work. Where the work is above ground level, the employer's written authorisation is needed in addition to any licence the state or territory requires. This is working practice in this course, not a checked legal rule. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on a roof or on a solar system.

instruction.heading: Quality is measured against the agreed scope
instruction.body: The quality of a pressure clean is judged against the scope the client agreed in writing, and against the test area that was agreed before the main work began. How bright a surface looks from the doorway is not the measure. A surface can look clean while residue is still present, while a sealed or fragile finish has been damaged, or while a sealant has lifted at an edge. Inspection should take place after the surface has dried enough to show its true state, because wet surfaces hide residue, water marks and lifted edges. The inspection checks the agreed scope, the preserved finish, the safe condition of the site, the environmental controls, the return of access to the client and the client's acceptance. Each of these is recorded separately so that a gap in one area does not get lost in a general statement.

instruction.heading: Before and after evidence
instruction.body: Take the before photographs at the walk-through, before any water is used, and take the after photographs from the same positions, under similar light and once the surface has dried. Number each zone on a simple site plan and label every photograph with its zone number, the date and the time. Include a close-up of any defect, a wide view that shows where the defect sits, and the test patch before and after. Photograph only what the owner or site has agreed may be photographed, and store the images with the job record. Do not use a before photograph taken after the work started, and do not select only the best after photographs. A record that shows the whole zone, including the parts that did not change, is the one that stands up later.

instruction.heading: Inspection, limitations and missed areas
instruction.body: Inspect every zone in the same order, and check for missed areas, damage, chemical residue, staining, water marks, lifted edges and any change in colour or texture that was not there before. Compare the result with the documented test patch and the photographs. Record limitations honestly. If an area could not be cleaned without risk of damage, record it as a limitation with the reason, such as a fragile sealed finish, a failing render or paint that lifts under pressure. Use plain words for the result. Lightened is not removed, and a reduced stain is not gone. Describe what changed and what did not. Remove barriers only after slip hazards and residual runoff have been dealt with, and check the walkways before the client uses them.

instruction.heading: Property defects found before and during the work
instruction.body: Record any existing defect at the walk-through, before work starts. Typical examples include cracked render, loose tiles, open joints, lifted paint and a damaged downpipe. Record each defect with its location, a photograph and a short factual description. If a defect is found after the work, record it as found at the point of inspection, not as caused by the cleaning, unless the evidence shows that the cleaning caused it. Keep pre-existing defects in a separate list from any change the work made, so that the handover does not blur the two. Tell the client in writing about any defect that may need a licensed trade or a specialist assessment, and do not offer a repair you are not authorised to carry out.

instruction.heading: Waste, wash water and chemical records
instruction.body: Keep a waste record for each job. Note the products used, the quantity used where it is known, how the waste and wash water were handled, and where the waste went. Record the handling in the same form for every job so that the owner can compare them. Until the rules for the work site are confirmed, follow the site and council instructions, the product's safety data sheet and the supervisor's direction, and record each step taken.

instruction.heading: Client sign-off, quotes and extra work
instruction.body: Walk the client through the completed work, the exclusions, the limitations, the concerns and any recommended follow-up. Give the client a concise written account, then ask for written acceptance. Acceptance is the point at which the Western Australian consumer page treats a quote as binding. Work outside the accepted scope needs the client's agreement first, and the Northern Territory consumer page takes the same position on extra work. If the client asks for more work during the visit, record the request and the price, and get the client's written approval before the work is started. Do not treat a verbal comment such as that the surface looks fine as acceptance.

instruction.heading: Incidents, near misses and handover
instruction.body: Record any incident or near miss on the day it happens, even if nobody was hurt: a slip, a hose failure, a lance strike, a chemical splash, a property contact or a complaint from a neighbour. Report it to the supervisor through the business's incident procedure. Close the handover with the completed checklist, the before and after photographs, the waste record, the defect and limitation list, the signed client acceptance and the incident record, if any. Each item is filed against the job, and the worker signs the handover once every item is present.

procedure: Confirm that the agreed scope, the test patch record and the walk-through photographs are on the job file before the inspection starts.
Wait until the surface has dried enough to show its true state, then start the inspection from the same point as the walk-through.
Inspect each numbered zone for missed areas, damage, chemical residue, staining, water marks and lifted edges.
Compare each zone with the test patch and the before photographs, and note every change and every limitation.
Take the after photographs from the same positions as the before photographs, labelled with zone, date and time.
Record each existing defect separately from any change made by the work, with a photograph and location.
Complete the waste record: products used, how waste and wash water were handled and where the waste went.
Remove barriers only after slip hazards and residual runoff have been addressed, and check the access route.
Walk the client through the completed work, exclusions, limitations, concerns and recommended follow-up, then give a written account.
Obtain written client acceptance, and record any extra work the client has approved in writing.
Record any incident or near miss and report it through the business's incident procedure.
File the handover pack against the job and have the worker and supervisor sign it.

workedExamples.situation: A client asks for a second, more aggressive pass to remove deep staining from a fragile sealed stone area. The test patch shows that the sealant starts to lift at a higher setting.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the first safe action, and who must be told?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not increase the intensity. Show the client the test patch and the photographs, and explain the limitation in plain words: the sealed finish is at risk at a higher setting. Tell the supervisor, who can offer an approved alternative or agree a limit. Record the request, the test result and the client's decision in writing. Any extra work needs the client's written approval before it starts, under the consumer rules in the safety notes. Do not claim the stain was removed unless the after inspection shows it.

workedExamples.situation: During the after inspection, a worker finds a dry corner of a rendered wall that was missed. The corner is still stained by a previous product.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should be recorded, and can the worker say the job is complete?
workedExamples.reasoning: The job is not complete for that zone. Record the missed corner as an open item with its location and a photograph. If the supervisor agrees that the corner is within scope, the worker can clean it, dry it, re-inspect it and add the new after photograph with its time. Record the change as a dated addition to the handover, and do not replace the first note. If the corner is outside the agreed scope, record it as an exclusion and tell the client.

workedExamples.situation: Three days after a job, a client says that a crack in the render was caused by the pressure clean. The walk-through photographs show the crack, and it was marked on the defect list before work started.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What evidence is shown, and what should the business avoid saying?
workedExamples.reasoning: Show the walk-through photograph and the defect entry, with its date and location. Explain that the crack was recorded before the work began. Do not say that the cleaning could not have affected the render, and do not say that it did. Record the client's concern, what the file shows and what remains uncertain. Offer a specialist assessment as a separate agreement if the client asks for one, and note it on the job file.

equipmentAndPpe: Camera or phone for photographs, used only with the owner's or site's permission
Site plan with numbered zones and an inspection checklist
Test patch record sheet with the setting, the surface, the result and the photographs
Barrier tape, cones and signs for the exclusion zone and the access route
Labelled waste bags and containers, and a waste record form
Written client acceptance form and a form for approved extra work
Safety glasses, gloves and safety footwear as the site risk assessment sets them for the inspection

commonErrors.error: Taking the after photographs before the surface has dried, or from different positions from the before photographs.
commonErrors.prevention: Inspect after drying, and take each after photograph from the position of the matching before photograph.

commonErrors.error: Reporting a surface as fully clean when it has only been lightened.
commonErrors.prevention: Describe what changed and what did not, and compare with the test patch.

commonErrors.error: Recording a pre-existing defect as caused by the cleaning, or the reverse.
commonErrors.prevention: Record each defect as found at the walk-through or inspection, and keep the defect list separate from the change list.

commonErrors.error: Removing barriers before slip hazards and residual runoff are addressed.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the walkways and the runoff first, then remove the barriers.

commonErrors.error: Accepting a verbal comment that the job looks fine as the client's sign-off.
commonErrors.prevention: Get written acceptance and record any extra work approved in writing.

commonErrors.error: Leaving an incident or near miss out of the handover because nobody was hurt.
commonErrors.prevention: Record every incident and near miss on the day it happens, and file it with the handover.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on a roof, from an elevated work platform or on a solar system, and completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. In New South Wales, a boom-type elevating work platform needs a WP high risk work licence where its boom length is 11 metres or more, so a shorter boom may not need it in that state (SafeWork NSW, High risk work licences, last modified 15 June 2026 per page metadata). Western Australia, where the WP licence covers a boom length of 11 metres or more (WorkSafe WA, last updated 13 August 2026); Tasmania, where the WP class covers booms of 11 metres or more (WorkSafe Tasmania, check the classes, last updated 1 December 2023); and the Northern Territory, where the licence class covers a boom length of 11 metres or more (NT WorkSafe bulletin, no date shown). In Queensland, the WorkSafe QLD page, search snippet, date not shown, says that elevated work platforms less than 11 metres in length are not included in the boom-type definition. Whether a boom-length threshold applies in Victoria is not confirmed by an official source. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Check the rule for the state or territory of the work, and obtain written employer authorisation before any work above ground level.

Quotes and extra work: The Western Australian consumer page distinguishes a quote, which is binding once accepted, from an estimate, which is an approximate cost that can move. The same page says the tradesperson needs the customer's agreement before doing extra work, and that the customer does not carry the cost of work they did not authorise. The Northern Territory page says the customer does not have to pay for work outside the quote unless they approved it.

Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In New South Wales, electrical wiring work includes repairing and altering an installation, and the licensing page excludes electrical articles connected to an outlet. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.
Follow the site and council instructions and the product's safety data sheet until the rules are confirmed.
Record every incident and near miss on the day, and report it through the business procedure. The supervisor decides on any external notification.

qualityStandard: Each numbered zone is inspected after drying for missed areas, damage, chemical residue and unexpected change.
Results are compared with the documented test patch and the before photographs, and every limitation is recorded in plain words.
Barriers are removed only after slip hazards and residual runoff have been addressed.
The client receives a concise written account of completed work, exclusions, concerns and recommended follow-up, and written acceptance is on file.
Pre-existing defects, waste records and incidents are each recorded and filed with the job.
documentationEvidence: Before and after photograph set, labelled by zone, date and time, with the owner's or site's permission
Completed inspection checklist and test patch record
Defect list, with pre-existing defects kept separate from work-related changes
Waste record showing products, handling and disposal route
Written client acceptance and any written approval for extra work
Incident or near-miss record, or a note that none occurred
summary: Quality is measured against the agreed scope and the test patch, after the surface has dried.
Before and after evidence is taken from the same positions and labelled, and limitations are recorded in plain words.
Pre-existing defects, waste records, client sign-off, extra work and incidents are each recorded separately and filed with the job.
A quote that is accepted binds the business and the client, and extra work needs the client's permission first.

knowledgeChecks.question: What must be verified before the handover is signed for a pressure clean?
options: The surface looks bright from the doorway, so the work is accepted by the client on the day
The inspection was done after drying, against the agreed scope, with limitations and concerns recorded
The barriers are removed before slip hazards and runoff are addressed on the job site today
The client gave a verbal assurance that everything is fine with the work and the finish

knowledgeChecks.question: A stain has been lightened but not fully removed. How should the handover describe it?
options: As removed, because it is no longer obvious to the eye at the handover of the job today
As lightened, with the reduction described and the remaining mark recorded as a limitation
Left out, because the client did not ask about it at the handover or the walk
As the previous owner's problem, not part of the clean job for the day at the site

knowledgeChecks.question: During the job the client asks for extra work that is not in the quote. What is correct?
options: Start the extra work, because it is a small change and the client will agree later
Record the request and the price, and get the client's written approval before starting
Charge for it afterwards without telling the client, since the work is already done
Ask the neighbour to confirm the client wants it before the work starts today
